subtitle: Lesson 20 · Joins, Subqueries & Set Operations

eyebrow: The ANSI syntax you already know
code:
-- T-SQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL — ANSI is the ONLY syntax
SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerName
FROM Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN Customers AS c
  ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID;
caption: T-SQL, MySQL, and PostgreSQL have never had any other way to write a join.

code:
-- Oracle — legacy (+) syntax for a LEFT JOIN
SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_name
FROM orders o, customers c
WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id(+);
caption: (+) marks the side allowed to be missing — still seen in older Oracle code.

eyebrow: (+) can't express a full outer join
code:
-- WHERE o.customer_id(+) = c.customer_id(+)  -- ORA-01468

-- ANSI handles it directly:
FULL OUTER JOIN customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;
caption: Putting (+) on both sides is illegal — one real limitation ANSI doesn't have.

code:
-- Oracle supports (+) for backward compatibility only.
-- Oracle itself recommends ANSI JOIN ... ON —
-- the same syntax as T-SQL, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.
caption: Write ANSI joins everywhere in this course, on every platform.
